title: Debloat observability agent and introduce attribute-prefilter cache
creator: Maya Liu
description: Reduce memory and CPU impact of the in-process observability agent used by the serving runtime. Current agent allocations spike on high-concurrency workloads due to expensive attribute normalization and JSON encoding. This ticket implements a two-part refactor: (1) a lightweight attribute-prefilter cache that deduplicates common label sets and applies fast-path canonicalization, and (2) a replace JSON encoder hotpath with a low-allocation, streaming encoder used only for non-sampled traces/logs. Goal is to lower p95 CPU contribution and heap by at least 30% under our synthetic traffic profile.
acceptance_criteria: Agent p95 CPU contribution reduced >= 30% on runtime-1.20 perf harness compared to baseline
Heap allocations attributed to agent decreased >= 35% during 1000 concurrent requests loadtest
End-to-end trace/metric/export path remains OTLP-compatible and passes integration tests
No increase in tail latency for user RPCs beyond 2% during traffic spike tests
Feature gated behind feature flag telemetry.debloat_v1 and gradual rollout plan exists
proposed_approach: Add attribute-prefilter cache: small fixed-size LRU keyed by attribute signature (stable hashing of attribute names+types) to deduplicate attribute vectors before normalization
Introduce compact attribute canonical form: intern string keys into shared string-pool and store attribute sets as compact byte ranges to avoid repeated map allocations
Replace JSON wide-encoder in hotpath with streaming encoder that emits OTLP-compatible protobuf bytes with zero-copy where possible; fallback to JSON only when explicitly requested
Expose feature flag telemetry.debloat_v1 with rollout percent and per-tenant override in console
Add unit tests for canonicalization logic, new encoder, and an integration test that validates downstream exporters (Honeycomb/Datadog) receive identical semantic payloads
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: canonicalization bugs could drop attributes or change keys - Mitigation: exhaustive property tests and cross-checks against golden export files

Risk: new LRU cache might introduce contention on extremely high cardinality workloads - Mitigation: per-worker sharded caches with adaptive eviction and telemetry to monitor hit/miss and lock contention
Risk: third-party exporters expect JSON structure - Mitigation: verify OTLP protobuf equivalence and provide a compatibility translation layer controlled by flag
Risk: rollout causes subtle downstream regressions - Mitigation: staged rollout (5/25/50/100%) with rollback hook and increased sampling for early adopters
rollout_plan: Stage 0: merge behind feature flag, run internal canaries (dev + staging) with telemetry validation
Stage 1: enable for 5% of production hostpool for 24h with elevated trace sampling
Stage 2: 25% for 48h if no regressions, collect memory/CPU metrics and exporter compatibility logs
Stage 3: 50% for 72h, run end-to-end synthetic workload to validate tail latency
Stage 4: global enable and mark feature stable, schedule follow-up to iterate on cache sizing
